Let
\[
u=T_1-I,\qquad v=T_2-I,\qquad w=T_3-I.
\]
Since \(n\) is a power of \(p\),
\[
T_i^n=I,\qquad (T_i-I)^n=0,
\]
so the function space is the group algebra
\[
R=\mathbb F_p[u,v,w]/(u^n,v^n,w^n).
\]

Put
\[
s=u+v+w.
\]
The equation \((T_1+T_2+T_3-3I)f=0\) is simply
\[
sf=0.
\]
Now \(w=s-u-v\), and because \(n\) is a \(p\)-power,
\[
w^n=(s-u-v)^n=s^n-u^n-v^n,
\]
so
\[
R\cong \mathbb F_p[u,v,s]/(u^n,v^n,s^n).
\]
Thus
\[
\ker(s)=s^{n-1}\mathbb F_p[u,v]/(u^n,v^n).
\]

Let
\[
q=\frac np,\qquad x=u^q,\qquad y=v^q.
\]
On \(\ker(s)\), we have
\[
w^q=(s-u-v)^q=s^q-u^q-v^q=-x-y,
\]
because \(s^q s^{n-1}=0\). Hence on \(\ker(s)\),
\[
A=xy+y(-x-y)+(-x-y)x=-(x^2+xy+y^2),
\]
and
\[
B=xy(-x-y)=-x^2y-xy^2.
\]

So the remaining two equations depend only on \(x,y\), where
\[
x^p=y^p=0.
\]
Write
\[
a=-(x^2+xy+y^2),\qquad b=-xy(x+y).
\]
The equations are
\[
(a^2+b^3+b^5)g=0,
\]
\[
((1+a+b)(a^2+b^3)+b^5)g=0.
\]
Subtracting gives
\[
(a+b)(a^2+b^3)g=0.
\]
Equivalently, in the quotient algebra for the annihilator count, we impose
\[
a^2+b^3+b^5=0,\qquad b^5(a+b)=0.
\]

Now \(a,b\) are the elementary symmetric invariants of \(x,y,-x-y\). The polynomial algebra \(\mathbb F_p[x,y]\) is free of rank \(6\) over \(\mathbb F_p[a,b]\). A convenient coinvariant basis has dimension \(6\), and under the cyclic rotation \((x,y,-x-y)\mapsto(y,-x-y,x)\), its nontrivial trace is \(0\), so its invariant part has dimension \(2\).

It remains to count the local quotient
\[
L=\mathbb F_p[a,b]/(a^2+b^3+b^5,\ b^5(a+b)).
\]
From \(b^5(a+b)=0\),
\[
b^5a=-b^6.
\]
Multiplying by \(a\) and using \(a^2=-b^3-b^5\),
\[
b^5a^2=-b^6a
\]
gives
\[
-b^8-b^{10}=b^7,
\]
so
\[
b^7(1+b+b^3)=0.
\]
Since \(1+b+b^3\) has constant term \(1\), it is a unit in the nilpotent local algebra, hence
\[
b^7=0.
\]
Thus \(L\) has basis
\[
1,b,\dots,b^6,\qquad a,ab,\dots,ab^4,
\]
so
\[
\dim_{\mathbb F_p}L=7+5=12.
\]

Therefore the quotient by the two polynomial constraints has dimension
\[
6\cdot 12=72,
\]
and its cyclic-invariant part has dimension
\[
2\cdot 12=24.
\]

Finally,
\[
\mathbb F_p[u,v]/(u^n,v^n)
\]
is a free module of rank \(q^2\) over
\[
\mathbb F_p[x,y]/(x^p,y^p),
\]
using residue classes \(u^r v^s\) with \(0\le r,s<q\). The cyclic trace on this residue factor is \(1\), so the invariant annihilator dimension scales by exactly \(q^2\). Hence
\[
\dim_{\mathbb F_p}V_n=24q^2.
\]

Since \(q=n/p\), the final answer is
\[
\boxed{24\left(\frac np\right)^2}.
\]
